items.title: Kyutai trains Pocket TTS's sampler with a 'drifting' objective, cutting inference to one step
items.summary: Kyutai published a new training technique for its open, CPU-only Pocket TTS model: instead of flow matching, the sampler head is trained with a 'drifting' objective, letting it generate audio in a single step with no Jacobian calculation, at the same quality as before. The training recipe and a new 'english_drifting_26-09' checkpoint are up on GitHub.
items.whyItMatters: A single-step, lower-compute decoding path for an open, CPU-capable TTS model is exactly the kind of latency/cost win worth tracking for a cheap or on-device fallback voice for Anna or Romain, on top of Kyutai's earlier French-normalization fix to the same model.

items.title: Modulate raises $25M for its audio-native, 100+ small-model voice analysis suite
items.summary: Boston startup Modulate raised $25M (led by Future Ventures, with Hyperplane and Lakestar) for a voice-intelligence platform that runs over 100 small, audio-native models — rather than one monolithic LLM — to handle transcription, emotion/intent analysis, deepfake detection, and compliance for voice agents in regulated industries.
items.whyItMatters: Its pitch that many small audio-native models beat one big LLM, and don't need specialized hardware, is a pattern worth borrowing if Romain or Anna ever need bolt-on emotion or safety checks without bloating the core real-time voice pipeline's cost.

items.title: Viral AI phone/text agent Instinct raises $1B Series C at a $10B valuation
items.summary: Instinct, an invite-only personal AI agent that calls and texts businesses on a user's behalf to book, buy, or cancel things, raised a $1B Series C from Sequoia, Benchmark, and Coatue at a $10B valuation — roughly 4x the valuation of its Series B just a month earlier.
items.whyItMatters: Not language-learning, but a useful data point on how aggressively investors are now pricing voice/phone-calling AI agents, the same product category Romain and Anna sit in.
